resources.string: Plug an ELM327 adapter into the OBD-II port (usually under the steering column) and switch the ignition on. The engine does not have to run, but RPM, air flow and temperatures only appear once it does.

Pair the adapter in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings first (the usual PIN is 1234 or 0000). Only paired devices are listed: scanning for new ones would require location access, which diagnostics does not need.
Wi-Fi adapters create their own network — join it in the phone settings. The usual address is 192.168.0.10, port 35000.
A virtual car inside the app: every screen works without an adapter or a vehicle. The data is plausible but not real.
Bluetooth is off or unsupported on this device
No paired devices. Pair the adapter in Bluetooth settings and come back.
Android 12 and newer require a separate permission before the app can talk to paired devices.
Lost the adapter: it was unplugged, the ignition went off, or the bus went quiet.
A shorter interval makes the gauges livelier. Cheap adapters start dropping answers when pushed — if values freeze, increase it.
Send a command straight to the adapter: ATI for the version, ATRV for voltage, 010C for RPM. The reply is shown as is.
No adapter connected. Open the Link tab and connect — or switch on demo mode to see the app without a car.
What to show on the gauges
The list holds only what this car reports. The remaining standard parameters are not supported by it.
No faults: the ECU has not stored a single code.
The ECU saw the fault once and is waiting to see whether it repeats — the lamp is not on yet.
These cannot be cleared by hand: the ECU clears them itself after several clean drive cycles.
Manufacturer-specific code: the exact meaning depends on the make.

Clearing turns the Check Engine lamp off and erases the stored codes together with the freeze frame, but it does not fix the cause: if the fault is still there, the code returns within a drive or two.\n\nIt also resets the readiness monitors — the car will fail an emissions test until the ECU has run them again.
The ECU refused the clear command
What the engine was doing when the ECU stored the fault.
All monitors complete — ready for an emissions test
This car does not report a VIN: service 09 is not supported by every ECU.
Taken from the 10th VIN character. The year code repeats every 30 years, so cars from the 1980s may be off by one cycle.
VIN check digit does not match — the VIN was read incorrectly
This VIN carries no check digit (it is mandatory for North America only)
Recording has not started. Data is logged while the app is connected to the adapter.

Distance and fuel come from the car itself — speed and air flow, no GPS. Fuel from air flow is an estimate: on a cold engine and at full throttle the ECU enriches the mixture, so real consumption is higher.
The file is ready. On Android 9 writing to the Downloads folder would need an extra permission — send the CSV to yourself with Share.

BLE adapters (Bluetooth 4.0 and newer) usually are not paired in advance and do not show up in the paired list - scanning finds them. A classic ELM327, in contrast, has to be paired once in the phone settings.
This phone has no Bluetooth Low Energy
On Android 8–11 the system cannot scan for BLE devices without precise location access: Bluetooth beacons can reveal where you are. The app does not need, read or send your location.
If the link drops (ignition off, you walked away), the app retries on its own - up to three times.
Gears are learned while driving: %1$d so far
Acceleration and braking are measured automatically from vehicle data. Bus speed arrives as whole km/h a few times per second - enough to compare your own runs, not to argue with the brochure.
Come to a stop and pull away - the run starts by itself.
Power is derived from mass, acceleration and drag. Road gradient and wind are ignored and mass comes from the profile - so this is an estimate for comparing runs, not a dyno figure.
Range, power estimate and gauge scales depend on these numbers - the OBD-II bus does not report them. Set them once for your car.
Does not look like a tyre size - expected 245/70R16

Manufacturers add their own parameters in service 22 - gearbox oil temperature, for instance. If you know the number and formula for your car, enter them and the parameter appears on the gauges. Service 01 is standard parameters, 22 is extended.
In a formula A, B, C… are the reply bytes in order; + - * / and brackets are available. Example: (A*256+B)/4
Check the fields - the formula or PID number could not be parsed

You do not need to turn mobile data off: the app binds the connection to the adapter network. If the phone leaves that network on its own (\"no internet access\"), tell it not to in the Wi-Fi settings for this network.
Connection bound to the adapter network
Could not bind the connection to the adapter network. If no data arrives, switch mobile data off while diagnosing.

Auto-detect always works, but cheap adapters redo the search on every connection. A 2016+ Patriot uses CAN 11 bit / 500 kbit/s — naming it directly saves a few seconds. If it turns out wrong, the app falls back to auto-detect.
Type what the repair manual for your car says. This text replaces the built-in one and survives a restart.
A description table from a file: one code per line, separated by a tab or a semicolon. An Excel export and a windows-1251 file both work.
No codes found in that file. It needs to be a text file with one code per line: P1513\tdescription
